title: Steam Session Length vs Achievement Yield
dataSources: Steam activity and achievements (`steam:activity`), Chess.com games (`chesscom:game`), online-go matches (`ogs:game`), and poker home-game hands or settlements (`pokerhome:session`).
app: Gaming and play telemetry from Steam, Chess.com, Online-Go servers, and poker home-game logs sent to Splunk HEC via APIs and export files.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=steam:activity
| search session_min=* achievements_unlocked=*
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(session_min) as avg_session_min avg(achievements_unlocked) as avg_achievements_unlocked by _time game_name
| sort - _time
description: Tracks achievement yield per Steam session over time and breaks it out by game.
value: Session length next to unlock yield makes it easier to see which games reward focused sessions versus endless grind.
implementation: Send achievement yield per Steam session events to `index=personal` with the fields used in the breakdown and review the resulting trend at 1w granularity.
visualization: Stacked time chart of achievement yield per Steam session by game.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Games & Tabletop — typical feeds: Video-game sessions (`game:session`), achievement unlocks (`achievement:unlock`), board-game plays (`boardgame:play`), chess games (`chess:game`), dice rolls (`dice:roll`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `steam:activity`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=steam:activity`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Gaming and tabletop telemetry — Steam / PSN / Xbox playtime and achievement APIs, BoardGameGeek plays export, Lichess / Chess.com game archives, and tabletop dice-roller logs — streamed to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs..

**Author notes:** Send achievement yield per Steam session events to `index=personal` with the fields used in the breakdown and review the resulting trend at 1w granularity.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "steam:activity", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:activity earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Steam Session Length vs Achievement Yield** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=steam:activity`) across the full search range. The `avg` aggregation groups by `_time`, `game_name`; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `game_name`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:activity
| search session_min=* achievements_unlocked=*
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(session_min) as avg_session_min avg(achievements_unlocked) as avg_achievements_unlocked by _time game_name
| sort - _time
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:activity earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, game_name
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=steam:activity earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.29.27: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Stacked Time Chart Of Achievement Yield Per Steam Session By Game (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `steam:activity` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=steam:activity | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1w` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1w` buckets.
